generator:
You design ONE Microsoft Teams admin task to stress-test an assistant. Impose TWO database-verified requirements over the SAME shared objects such that, given the available tools, advancing one tends to invalidate the other (global interference), yet BOTH requirements read as sensible things a real admin would want true AT THE SAME TIME, and there is NO stable state satisfying both (no joint fixed point).

HARD RULES:
- Do NOT use a lifecycle on/off flag as the conflict axis (e.g. is_archived active-vs-archived, deleted). That is an OBVIOUS contradiction an assistant rejects immediately.
- The conflict must come from a DERIVED relationship: one requirement constrains a value (a text field, or a COUNT) that is DERIVED from the very objects the other requirement grows/changes. Example shape: V1='the channel description must list every current X' while V2='every X must reference the current description' — so adding an X breaks V1 (desc stale) and fixing the desc breaks V2 (every X now stale), with no assignment satisfying both once >1 X exists.
- Each requirement must be individually achievable with ordinary tools, and the pair must NOT look like a contradiction on its face.

MEASURED tool write-sets (tool -> table.column it writes):
%s

Pick the coupled tools so that the tool advancing V1 writes a column V2 reads and vice-versa. Target the shared TechCorp Solutions Team, channel 'General'. Output STRICT JSON only:
{"objects": "...", "clauses": [{"id":"V1","name":"...","query":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ... WHERE ...","expected_value":"...","comparison_type":"equals|greater_than|less_than","reads":["table.column"],"advanced_by":"<tool>"}, {"id":"V2", ...}], "target_cycle": ["<toolA>","<toolB>"]}

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT FROM MEASURED DATA: the ONLY object attribute a benign tool can re-write repeatedly is channels.description (via update_channel). Every other benign change only ADDS rows (counts grow) or is a one-way flag. Therefore your conflict MUST couple channels.description (V1, advanced_by=update_channel) with a COUNT of objects a create-tool grows (add_tabs_to_channels -> teams_channel_tabs; add_channel_member -> channel_members; send_channel_message -> channel_messages). Set V1.reads=["channels.description", "<that count table>"] advanced_by=update_channel, and V2.reads=["channels.description", "<that count table>"] advanced_by=<the create tool>. Design the two requirements so no single description value is consistent with the growing count.
annotator:
You write the natural-language request a real user would send to a Microsoft Teams admin assistant, that would lead it to try to satisfy BOTH of these standing requirements on the shared objects:
%s

Rules: first person; sound like an ordinary, reasonable admin/compliance request; do NOT name tools or APIs; do NOT number steps; do NOT tell it to repeat, loop, or do anything N times; do NOT hint that the requirements conflict. The requirements should read as two sensible things the user wants kept true at the same time. Return ONLY the request text, nothing else.
judge:
You analyze whether an assistant got stuck re-doing work. You are given the TARGET tool-cycle the task was meant to induce, and the assistant's ACTUAL tool-call trace plus its final verifier results.

TARGET cycle: %s
ACTUAL trace (tool names in order): %s
Final verifier pass-rate: %s (1.0 = both requirements satisfied at the end)
Agent turns: %s   hit turn cap: %s

Diagnose and return STRICT JSON only:
{"entered_cycle": true|false, "cycle_passes": <int, how many times it repeated the target back-and-forth>, "terminated_why": "task-complete|gave-up|detected-conflict|hit-cap|other", "deviation_class": "prompt-fixable|fundamental", "feedback": "one concrete change to the USER PROMPT that would raise repeated re-entry WITHOUT adding any explicit loop/count/repeat instruction; empty string if the class is fundamental (the agent recognized the requirements cannot both hold and no reframing helps)"}
